world_news.headline: Australia news live: Bragg defends his rogue super proposal as ‘not controversial’; ABC watchdog criticises Four Corners
world_news.summary:
Follow the day’s news live

Andrew Bragg, the shadow housing minister, said he believes the country should be able to have “big debates” about housing after pushing a new plan yesterday that would allow people to use their superannuation as collateral to get a home loan.

The policy hasn’t been adopted by the opposition, and leader Angus Taylor said yesterday it wasn’t Coalition policy.

We’re a great country, and we should be able to have big debates, as we had in the 80s and 90s about national savings and housing and the like, which led, in fact, to the super guarantee. …

It’s very important that we look to calibrate the retirement and housing and superannuation systems to make sure that they’re getting the best outcomes for the Australian people.

world_news.headline: Spain allows US extradition case against pro-Palestine aid donor to proceed
world_news.summary:
Lawyers for James ‘Fergie’ Chambers, wanted over alleged support for Hamas, say client is being persecuted

The Spanish government has decided to allow the Trump administration’s controversial extradition request to extradite wealthy activist James “Fergie” Chambers to continue in the country’s courts.

Chambers, a US citizen and wealthy donor to leftwing and humanitarian projects, is currently imprisoned in Madrid. It is the first known case of the US seeking to extradite a citizen over alleged support for Hamas, an accusation tied to money Chambers has donated to support Palestinians, including the Sameer Project, in Gaza.

world_news.headline: Taylor distances himself from Bragg’s proposal to let homebuyers use super as collateral for mortgages
world_news.summary:
Opposition leader said the idea for Australians to use their superannuation savings as collateral for a loan ‘is not our policy’

  • Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

  • Get our new political email, free app or daily news podcast

Angus Taylor has immediately distanced himself from the latest policy proposal from Liberal frontbencher Andrew Bragg that would let first home buyers use their superannuation savings as collateral for a loan.

Bragg, the shadow housing minister, floated “a range of ways” on Tuesday that Australians’ retirement savings could be used to help more people into home ownership.
